senses.gloss: f. (זרד) bushes of sorb, or service-tree, growing in unhealthy marshes (v. Löw. Pfl. p. 289) Pes. 111ᵇ דבי ז׳ שידי (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 400) the spirits of the sorb-bushes are named shiddé (demons).
units: Ib. ז׳ סמיכא למתא וכ׳ a sorb-bush near a town has no less than sixty shiddé; [Ms. M. זַרְזְתָא, זִירְזְתָא, זַרְתָּא; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. notes).—

<cite ref="Kiddushin 73b:2">Kidd. 73ᵇ</cite> <he>ז׳ … יש בו וכ׳</he> a child exposed in a sorb-bush near a town (where it is likely to die) is considered a foundling (<cite ref="A02334"><he>אֲסוּפִי</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Ketubot 79a:13">Keth. 79ᵃ</cite> <he>אבא ז׳ וכ׳</he> a forest (of timber), a sorb plantation and a fish-pond.
